how.fitTitle: Start from how people actually work
how.fitBody: Seven years in customer support taught me where systems fail people. So I build for the real workflow: phone-only accounts when customers have no e-mail, a quote list when a shop has no prices yet.
how.proofBody: Strict TypeScript, tests next to the code, and CI that refuses a missing translation. This site is built the same way; the source is public.
how.docsBody: Handover notes after every build session, a findings list instead of silent fixes, and documentation that carried a team through a change in leadership.

about.heading: Hello, I’m Clérise.
about.intro: I think in systems. I am direct, practical, and happiest when I am solving a problem by building something.
about.story: For seven years I worked in remote customer support: player support for AAA games, then managing an international e-commerce team of 20 at Amazon, then leading escalations for mobile game launches. I kept running into the same thing: the people were fine, the systems around them were not. So I learnt to build them. I finished HyperionDev's full-stack bootcamp early, at the top of my cohort, and spent two years as a full-stack developer for a team in Amsterdam.
about.business: I also run my own businesses. HCreations Embroidery Blanks supplies blanks to embroiderers across South Africa; I run it with three women who work for me, and I rebuilt its shop myself. That mix of support, engineering and business is what I bring to a team: I know what the code is for.

looking.level: Intermediate level, front-end or full-stack, with Vue as my strongest tool. Roles that mix in tech lead or product work are welcome.
looking.where: Remote: South Africa or international, the Netherlands especially. My home office has backup power and a reliable connection.

about.offBody: I keep a journal to spot patterns. I build Pokémon TCG decks. I play puzzle, exploration, builder and automation games, and I paint with watercolours.
about.cs2: CS2? I like it. Or, well, no. But yes. But no.
